salient_findings: Confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques with overlying thick greasy scales
Superficial dermal band-like lymphocytic infiltrate with dermal fibrosis
key_facts: Previous treatment with oral prednisolone and cyclosporine without improvement
Skin punch biopsies showed epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes
Immunohistochemical staining showed tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO
CD30 was positive in fewer than 25% of lymphocytes

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes and dermal fibrosis are characteristic features

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of erythroderma and atypical lymphocytes with CD3 and CD45RO positivity

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphocytic infiltration and immunohistochemical staining pattern are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological features are similar to this variant of mycosis fungoides

shortlist.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the presence of atypical lymphocytes and CD30 positivity in a subset of cells warrants consideration of this rare diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of erythroderma, epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes, and immunohistochemical staining positive for CD3 and CD45RO are consistent with mycosis fungoides. The absence of palpable lymphadenopathy and the specific immunophenotype also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome typically presents with more systemic involvement and lymphadenopathy, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes mycosis fungoides, but the specific features of this case point more specifically to mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The absence of follicular involvement and the presence of epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and immunophenotype do not match adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, which typically has a more aggressive course and different immunophenotypic features.
